newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin repeats no broad tax cuts yet.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin repeats no broad tax cuts yet.

text.p: Finance Minister Paul Martin said on Tuesday he would not jeopardize Canada's deficit reduction efforts by introducing broad-based tax reductions too early.
"We want to bring down taxes and we intend to bring down taxes," Martin told reporters.

"In fact we've already begun with selective tax cuts. But in terms of broader-based tax reductions, we are not going to do it if there is any chance that the deficit would go up or if there is any chance that health care, education or old age pensions would be threatened as a result," he said.
"The fact of the matter is Canadians have made it very clear to all governments that they don't want to see dividends spent before they are earned.

"They want to see us lick the deficit very clearly. We've also said that there are social priorities on which money should be spent. And we set those priorities out in the budget very clearly and we've said we'd like to work on fuller funding as the money as the country can afford it."
As a federal election approaches, probably in June, the ruling Liberals have been under pressure by the tax-cutting pledges of the Conservative and Reform parties.
